result.topic_en: Notes on Pasteur's findings about optically active compounds: tartrates that are holohedral or hemihedral, and the claim that compounds differing only in opposite hemihedry or opposite rotation of the plane of polarization behave identically with inactive partners but differently with active ones (examples: tartaric acid, malic and aspartic acid, cinchonine, quinine, brucine, strychnine).

items.english: B. Compounds which, like right- and left-handed tartaric acid, differ only by opposite hemihedry or opposite rotation of the plane of polarization of light, give, when combined with compounds that do not act on light, symmetrically isomorphous compounds that are completely identical in their other physical and chemical properties, but when combined with active compounds, give compounds with essentially different chemical properties.
